# Ai Assistant

Use only the rules that apply to the current consumer task.

## Contents

- [Add a governed assistant with durable conversations and in-chat approvals](#add-a-governed-assistant-with-durable-conversations-and-in-chat-approvals)

## Add a governed assistant with durable conversations and in-chat approvals

Register agents over existing governed tools with AddNewHeapAssistant, persist conversations in the library-owned nhai schema, stream turns as server-sent events, let the user approve exact NewHeap proposals in the chat, share conversations with colleagues who continue them with their own permissions, follow them live and notify people who are away, and let administrators manage agents, MCP servers and the application context while users set style preferences.

## Preferred approach

Add `NewHeap.Platform.AI.Chat.AspNet` and exactly one storage package,
`NewHeap.Platform.AI.Chat.SqlServer` or `NewHeap.Platform.AI.Chat.PostgreSql`.
Register the application's own AI services first (chat profiles, generated tool
catalogs, discovery policy, verifiers), then `AddNewHeapPlatformAIAspNet`, and call
`AddNewHeapAssistant` last:

```csharp
services.AddNewHeapAssistant(assistant => assistant
    .UsePostgreSql(connectionString, options => { options.Schema = "nhai"; options.RunMigrations = true; })
    .UseAccessPolicy("app.assistant.access")
    .UseChatProfile("project-assistant-chat")
    .AddAgent(new NhAssistantAgentDefinition(
        Id: "project-assistant", Version: 1,
        DisplayNameKey: "nh-assistant.agents.project-assistant.name",
        DescriptionKey: "nh-assistant.agents.project-assistant.description",
        ProfileName: "project-assistant-chat",
        Instructions: NhAiTextAsset.FromEmbeddedResource(typeof(Agents).Assembly, "App.Agents.project-assistant.md", "project-assistant", 1),
        ToolSelectors: ["projects.*"],
        Autonomy: NhAiAutonomyLevel.Execute,
        RequiredPolicy: "app.project.view"))
    .AddBusinessAuditSink<ApplicationAssistantAuditSink>()
    .AddToolPresenter<ApplicationAssistantToolPresenter>()
    .WithLimits(limits => { limits.MaxToolCallsPerTurn = 8; limits.DailyToolCallBudgetPerActor = 200; }));

endpoints.MapNewHeapAssistant("/api/assistant");
```

`NhAiTextAsset.FromEmbeddedResource` is a static extension member of
`NewHeap.Platform.AI.Chat`; keep that namespace in scope. The chat profile must
declare chat, function calling and streaming and permit the assistant execution
region (`local` by default, see `UseExecutionRegion`). Tool selectors are exact tool
ids or prefixes ending in `.*`; only agents with `Execute` autonomy are offered
mutating tools. An agent may list at most `NhAssistantLimits.MaxToolSelectorsPerAgent`
selectors (128 by default) for code-defined and administrator-managed agents alike;
the application decides that number through `WithLimits`. Code agents are checked at
host start, administrator input on save. The selector list must also fit
`NhAssistantLimits.MaxStoredToolSelectorCharacters` (8,000 characters of JSON).
Prefer prefix selectors over long lists of exact ids, and remember that
`MaxToolsPerAgent` (64 by default) still bounds how many tools one turn offers.
To let a chat agent consult another agent about a subject, select the generated
`assistant.consult.{agentId}.{subjectType}` tool of an agent that allows consultation
(`nh-ai-agent-runs`); the consultation answers in the same turn with the chatting
person's rights. An agent is never offered its own consultation tool.

The kill switch is `NewHeap:AI:Assistant:Enabled` (default `false`). When it is
off, `GET status` reports `enabled: false` without agents and every other endpoint
returns `404`. Every endpoint requires the access policy
(`NewHeap:AI:Assistant:AccessPolicy`, default `app.assistant.access`); an agent's
`RequiredPolicy` is checked when the agent is listed, when a conversation is created
and before every turn.

A turn runs inside the HTTP request and streams `turn.started`, `message.delta`,
`tool.started`, `tool.completed`, `approval.required`, `turn.completed` or `error`,
with a `: keep-alive` comment every 15 seconds. A client disconnect or `POST cancel`
cancels the turn in the same process. Tools run as the signed-in user through the
application's invocation gate: the assistant decorates that gate so the agent acts
as a non-human actor on behalf of the accountable owner taken from the registered
`INhAiAuthenticatedInvocationContextResolver`, with the turn id as run id and the
instruction version and hash as prompt identity.

When the shared invoker requires approval, the assistant creates the exact
`NhAiProposal` from the arguments the invoker evaluated, stores it with a pending
approval, streams `approval.required` and pauses. The user decides with the
expected proposal hash. On approve, the same governed function runs again through
the invoker with the proposal and approval ids bound to the context, a durable
idempotency lease keyed by the proposal and the tool's verifier; on reject, the
model receives a rejected result and may close with one message. Expired
proposals end with `assistant-approval-expired`. A proposal lives for
`NhAssistantLimits.ApprovalLifetime` (15 minutes) on the application's clock (a
registered `TimeProvider`, otherwise the system clock): its expiry, the decision's
`DecidedAt`, the conversation's `expired` status and the invoker's validation all
read that clock, while `CreatedAt`, tool calls and audit events keep the system
clock. A test lets a proposal expire by moving its clock past the lifetime instead
of shortening the lifetime or waiting.

Use `AddToolPresenter<T>()` when a consumer can explain a tool with localized domain
names. The presenter receives the exact governed arguments, invocation context and
request culture. Resolve display data again inside the authorized scope, return a short
`NhAssistantApprovalPresentation`, and keep `NhAiToolDescriptor.Description` as English
model metadata. Presentation is bounded, persisted and optional; it never enters the
proposal hash or grants access. Failure, timeout, oversized output, confidential or
restricted classification, old stored data and an unhandled tool all use the safe
fallback. Never log presenter text, arguments or lookup results.

The library replaces `INhAiBudgetManager`, `INhAiIdempotencyManager` and
`INhAiApprovalEvidenceProvider` with durable implementations on its own tables.
Budget and evidence requests outside an assistant turn are delegated to the
implementations registered before `AddNewHeapAssistant`. Call
`UseApplicationBudgetInTurns()` when the application's budget manager must also reserve the
model and tool calls of assistant turns: once the assistant's daily budget accepted a call, the
application's manager receives it with the agent, skill, run and purpose (`chat`, `agent-run`,
`consultation` or `proposal-execution`), and its refusal ends the call as
`assistant-budget-exhausted`. Register that manager before `AddNewHeapAssistant`
(`UseBudgetManager<TManager>()` or `UseInMemoryBudget`); with only the default manager, which
refuses every reservation, host start fails.

## Administration and personalization

Register an admin policy with `UseAdminPolicy` (or `NewHeap:AI:Assistant:AdminPolicy`,
default `app.assistant.admin`); startup fails when it does not exist, because
`MapNewHeapAssistant` also maps the `admin/*` endpoints behind the access and admin
policies. `GET status` reports `canAdminister`. Every assistant endpoint (chat, administration,
agent runs, subjects, run histories, boards, MCP connections and the OAuth callback) answers a failure
as `{ code, messageKey, errors? }` with the one HTTP status the assistant gives that code, whichever
endpoint returns it: for example `assistant-validation` (`400`, camelCase field keys in `errors`,
dotted for nested input such as `oauth.clientSecretReference`), `assistant-forbidden` and
`assistant-context-unavailable` (`403`), the `*-not-found` codes (`404`), conflicts with the
current state (`409`), remote MCP and OAuth failures (`502`) and a failing secret store or a run that
could not be queued (`503`). `errors` carries field errors for any code, such as the parameters of an
invalid run filter. Clients map the code, never the status, to a text.

- **Agents.** Agents added with `AddAgent` are code agents: they are upserted into
  `AssistantAgent` at startup and stay the default. Administrators override, disable
  and reset them (the source stays `code`) and create their own agents. Every change
  carries `expectedVersion`; a stale version returns `409`. Tool selectors apply to
  local and bridge tools; MCP tools are assigned per server with `mcpServerIds`.
- **Application context.** `UseDefaultApplicationContext` seeds version 1 once; a
  changed seed never replaces an existing context. Administrators edit it with
  `expectedVersion`, and the history is kept.
- **Instructions.** Each turn composes, in order of authority, the fixed library
  rules, the application context, the agent instructions and the user's style
  preferences. Preferences (`style`, `addressForm`, `responseLength`) become fixed
  English or Dutch lines chosen from `Accept-Language`; custom instructions are
  bounded, neutralized and treated as style wishes only. The identity
  (`default@<version>+<asset>@<version>+preferences@<hash>`) and the SHA-256 of the
  composed text flow into the invocation context; the separate versions and hashes
  flow into `NhAssistantAuditEvent`. Editing the context or preferences while an
  approval is pending invalidates that approval.
- **MCP servers.** Configure `ConfigureMcp`: `RequireHttps` (plain http only to
  loopback in Development), optional `AllowedHosts`, exact `ForwardUserTokenHosts`,
  `ToolListCacheDuration` and `ConnectTimeout`. Secrets for `bearer` and `api-key`
  are protected with ASP.NET Data Protection and never returned (`hasSecret`), logged
  or audited; `forward-user-token` uses `INhAiCallerCredentialAccessor` only for
  allow-listed hosts. Synced tools start disabled as approval-required mutations;
  administrators activate them and may mark them read-only, and a changed input
  schema disables a tool again. Enabled tools of the servers assigned to an agent are
  imported per turn with `INhAiMcpClientToolImporter` (`mcp.<server>.<tool>`), so
  approval, idempotency, budget and audit apply unchanged. An unreachable server is
  skipped for the turn. The client attaches the credential to every HTTP request and
  checks each request against the planned origin and `AllowedHosts`; a `403` with
  `error="insufficient_scope"` reports `assistant-mcp-insufficient-scope`. A tool list
  seen with one caller's forwarded token never disables a tool for everyone; only an
  administrator's sync writes `missing` and `schema-changed`. Test, sync and turns
  with the shared credential record `lastConnectAt` and `lastConnectCode`; a test or sync with an
  administrator's own credential does not, because it says nothing about the server for everyone else.
- **MCP credentials.** Besides `none`, `bearer`, `api-key` and `forward-user-token`,
  a server can use `basic` (`userName` plus the write-only secret as password). A
  secret is stored with Data Protection or named by `secretReference`:
  `config:<name>` reads `NewHeap:AI:Assistant:Mcp:Secrets:<name>`, another prefix needs
  an `INhAssistantMcpSecretResolver` registered with `AddMcpSecretResolver<T>(prefix)`
  (for example a vault). A reference is resolved for every request, so a rotation applies
  at once; its name has no `:` or `..`, so it never reaches other configuration. The
  value is read with `NhConfigurationSecrets.Read` (also from the secrets files); a blank
  value or one with an unresolved `${...}` reference counts as missing. A stored secret
  and a reference replace each other. `clientCertificateReference` names
  a certificate under `NewHeap:AI:Assistant:Mcp:ClientCertificates:<name>` (`Path` and
  `Password` of a PKCS#12 file, or `Thumbprint` in a store) with a private key, which the
  client presents for mutual TLS. `transport` is `streamable-http`, or `auto` for a
  server that only offers the deprecated HTTP+SSE transport; the SSE `endpoint` event
  must stay on the configured origin. Saving a reference that names nothing available fails with the
  field error `not-found` at `secretReference`, `oauth.clientSecretReference` or
  `clientCertificateReference`; at runtime such a server is skipped with
  `assistant-mcp-secret-reference-invalid` or `assistant-mcp-certificate-reference-invalid`. A stored
  secret or client secret that no longer decrypts, for example after the data protection keys changed,
  fails with `409 assistant-mcp-secret-unreadable` and a warning: enter it again. A secret resolver that
  throws fails with `503 assistant-mcp-secret-unavailable` and its exception is logged.
- **MCP in background runs.** A server's tools are offered in headless runs (and in
  the execution of their deferred proposals) only when an administrator sets its
  `headlessUse` (`NhAssistantMcpHeadlessUses`); every server starts at `never`.
  `organization` is for `none`, `bearer`, `api-key` and `basic`: the server's own
  credential serves the run. The call is authorized like any agent call: with the
  initiator's rights (`Delegated`), the accountable account's rights (`Accountable`)
  or a code grant (`Grant("mcp.<server>.*")`), which such tools accept. `requiredPolicy`
  is checked for the person whose rights the run uses; a run that acts for the agent
  alone does not get servers with a required policy. An approved deferred proposal
  imports the tool again under the same rules and executes it once; a server that no
  longer allows headless use fails it with `assistant-mcp-headless-not-allowed`. A call whose request never
  left the host (a blocked target, a call the credential may not carry, a credential that could not be
  obtained) or that the server refused with `401` or `403` without a renewed credential certainly did
  not run: its approved proposal ends `execution-failed` with that code, never `execution-unknown`. A
  chat approval of a tool whose server is left out of the turn fails with the server's skip code, as a
  deferred execution does.
- **Personal servers in background runs.** `personal` is for `forward-user-token`
  first-party servers: a run sends a short-lived delegated NewHeap token of
  the person whose rights it uses (`INhAiMcpDelegatedTokenIssuer`, at most
  `ForwardedTokenLifetime`, two minutes by default and five at most), minted per request
  for hosts in `ForwardUserTokenHosts` only, marked with the invocation and bound to the
  server's origin. It needs that person's consent: `GET mcp-connections` lists the
  personal servers of agents the caller may use, `PUT mcp-connections/{serverId}`
  `{ allowBackgroundUse }` records or withdraws it, and a changed URL or authentication
  needs consent again. Without it the server is skipped with
  `assistant-mcp-consent-required`; a person who may not sign in, an issuer failure or a
  JWT bearer scheme of the host that does not restrict delegated tokens gives
  `assistant-mcp-delegated-token-unavailable`. A call that the gate authorized with any
  other grant source than that person's is refused with `assistant-mcp-credential-mismatch`
  before it is sent. Consent (`McpBackgroundUseChanged`) and issuing are audited without
  the token; issuing once per turn, server, person and outcome as `McpDelegatedTokenIssued`
  with `TokenCount`. The receiving server calls
  `AddNewHeapPlatformAIMcpDelegatedTokens(tokens => tokens.Accept(origin, "/mcp"))`; the
  assistant's own host accepts no such token. Sign the host's tokens asymmetrically
  (`NhJwtSigningKeys` with `ES256` or `RS256`, `nh-auth-token-signing`) and publish the keys with
  `MapNewHeapJwks`: the delegated token's `aud` is then the server's origin, and the server validates
  it with `UseNewHeapJwks(jwksUri, issuer, issuer, origin)` without a key that could mint tokens. With
  the shared HS256 key the token keeps the issuer as `aud` and every host that can validate it can also
  mint tokens; use that only between hosts that already share the key.
  A run that leaves such a server out records the server and the code on the run
  (`McpConnectionSkips` in the run history and result: consent required, connection or
  reauthorization required, or `assistant-mcp-initiator-only`), and the person whose consent or
  connection is missing is told with `NhAssistantAgentNotificationKind.McpConnectionMissing`, at most
  once per server and day; `UseInAppAgentNotifications` puts it in the application's inbox. Apply the
  `McpRunConnectionSkips` migrations.
- **MCP servers as readers.** An administrator gives a server readers that turn files into text for
  models that do not read their type (`readers` on the server, at most 16, stored in their own table;
  per reader `toolName`, a tool synced from the server, one reader per tool, so a new server gets its
  readers after a sync; `mediaTypes`, one to 16; `maxClassification`, the highest classification that
  may be sent to it; `priority`, -1000 to 1000, default 0; `NhAssistantMcpReaders`). The runtime, not
  the model, calls the reader's tool with `name`, `mediaType` and the base64 `content` of the file
  and gives the model the text blocks of its result; the tool need not be enabled for agents and the
  server need not be assigned to the agent. The readers of every server are asked after the
  application's own, by `priority`, highest first, then by server id and tool name. Sending a file to
  an MCP server is data leaving the platform, so everything is checked before the request: a file
  above the reader's `maxClassification` is refused with `assistant-classification-not-permitted`, a
  disabled server is ignored, `requiredPolicy` applies to the turn's person, and a headless turn
  follows the rules above: `headlessUse`, the person's consent for `personal`
  (`assistant-mcp-consent-required`) and `assistant-mcp-initiator-only`. A reader whose server cannot
  be planned or reached, or whose tool is gone or has another input schema than the synced one, is
  passed over with its code; once the request may have reached the tool, an error result, no text or
  a failure refuses the file with `assistant-file-reader-failed`. A personal OAuth server the person
  of a request turn has not connected, or must connect again, shows that person the same
  `connection-required` card as its tools; an attachment it refused stays in the message, so asking
  again after connecting reads it. Headless runs show no card and keep their notices. `readers: null`
  or omitted keeps the readers, `[]` removes them all; validation reports `readers` (`too-long`) and
  per reader with its index `readers[0].mediaTypes` (`required`, `invalid`, `too-long`),
  `readers[0].toolName` (`required`, `invalid` also for a second reader of the same tool,
  `not-found`), `readers[0].maxClassification` (`required`, `invalid`) and `readers[0].priority`
  (`invalid`). Apply the `McpServerReaders` and `McpReaders` migrations; the second moves a server's
  reader setting into its own reader at priority 0.
- **Authentication modes of the application.** An identity flow the built-in modes do not cover,
  such as a token exchange with the application's identity provider, is a provider in code:
  implement `INhAssistantMcpCredentialProvider` (`GetAsync` returns the headers of the next request
  as `NhAssistantMcpCredential`, `RenewAsync` after a `401` when `CanRenew`, `AuthorizeCall` decides
  which governed calls may carry it) and register it with
  `AddMcpCredentialProvider<TProvider>(mode, ownership)`. `NhAssistantMcpCredentialOwnership.Organization`
  shares one credential and allows `headlessUse: organization`; `Person` sends each person's own
  credential (`NhAssistantMcpCredentialSubject.PersonActorId`), is never shared, allows `headlessUse:
  personal` with the person's consent and authorizes calls with
  `NhAssistantMcpCredentialProviders.AuthorizePersonalCall`. Return expected refusals with
  `NhAssistantMcpCredentialProviders.Failed(code)`; never log a credential. The provider is a
  singleton that reads its own configuration; a server of the mode takes no secret in the editor, and
  `GET admin/mcp-auth-modes` lists the registered modes for it.
- **MCP servers with OAuth.** `oauth-client-credentials` connects the organization with
  the host's own client (`oauth.clientId` with a write-only `clientSecret`, a
  `clientSecretReference` or, for `private_key_jwt`, the `clientCertificateReference`);
  the first use obtains a token. `oauth` with `connectionScope: organization` needs an
  administrator to authorize the organization's account once, named by
  `organizationAccountLabel` because everyone using the server's agents then acts as it.
  Before saving, `POST admin/mcp-servers/discover` shows what the server's challenge and
  protected resource metadata (RFC 9728) name; saving with `oauth.confirmAuthorization`
  pins that issuer and the canonical resource, and a new server or address needs it.
  Tokens are requested from the pinned issuer only, always with `resource`; PKCE `S256`
  is required and the `iss` of the redirect is checked (RFC 9207). A server that later
  names another authorization server suspends its connections (`issuer-changed`) until
  an administrator confirms again. Configure `NhAssistantMcpOptions.OAuth`:
  `RedirectUri` is the public `<prefix>/mcp/oauth/callback` (required for `oauth`,
  otherwise `assistant-mcp-oauth-not-configured`), `ReturnOrigins` the origins of the
  pages that start an authorization, and optionally `ClientMetadataDocumentUri` for
  `<prefix>/mcp/oauth/client-metadata.json`; without a client id the host uses that
  document or registers itself dynamically, once per issuer, and again when the registration's client
  secret expired or the authorization server answers `invalid_client` (a connection whose refresh token
  belonged to that registration then needs a new authorization). The administrator starts
  with `POST admin/mcp-servers/{id}/connection/authorize` and opens the URL in a popup;
  the anonymous callback exchanges the code and its page posts a one-time completion
  code to the opener, which `POST mcp-connections/complete` turns into the connection
  with the starter's own session and the admin policy. A failure reaches the browser as `code` and
  `messageKey` in the message to the opener, or as `nh-mcp-error` and `nh-mcp-message-key` in the
  return URL's fragment in redirect mode, and the callback never answers a bare `500`. Every connection
  endpoint follows one rule: authorizing needs `oauth`, the organization's connection exists for `oauth`
  and `oauth-client-credentials`, personal connections only for `oauth` with `connectionScope: user`;
  anything else answers `409 assistant-mcp-connection-not-supported`. Tokens are protected with Data
  Protection, renewed once across instances before expiry (a database lease) and after a
  `401`; `insufficient_scope` asks client credentials for the union of scopes within
  `oauth.scopes` (`assistant-mcp-scope-not-allowed` otherwise). A refused refresh ends
  the connection with `assistant-mcp-reauthorization-required`. Disconnecting
  (`DELETE .../connection`), changing the address, mode, scopes, client or issuer, and
  deleting the server revoke the tokens (RFC 7009). Discovery, metadata and token
  endpoints pass the host guard and never reach private networks unless the host is in
  `AllowedHosts`; `BlockPrivateNetworks` applies that to MCP servers too. Connecting,
  disconnecting and ending are audited (`McpConnection*`) without tokens.
- **Personal MCP connections.** `oauth` with `connectionScope: user` lets each person connect
  their own account: `POST mcp-connections/{serverId}/authorize` (with `allowBackgroundUse` to
  consent to background use when the server's `headlessUse` is `personal`), completed with the
  person's own session, and `DELETE mcp-connections/{serverId}` revokes it; a consent stays until
  the person withdraws it. `GET mcp-connections` reports `connectionStatus`, scopes and
  `offersBackgroundUse`. A request turn uses the connection of the person who sent the message, also
  in a shared conversation; without one the turn goes on without the server, the model is told the
  service is not connected, and the turn streams `connection.required` (`serverId`, `displayName`,
  `reason`: `NhAssistantMcpConnectionReasons`), which is stored as a `connection-required` part. A
  server that refuses the connection's scopes records them and asks with `insufficient-scope`;
  connecting again requests them. A headless run uses the person whose rights it uses only with
  `personal` headless use and that person's consent, and an approved proposal executes with the
  connection of the person who asked (Q10) or fails with `assistant-mcp-connection-required`. A
  headless turn a person asked for uses only that person's own connection, with their consent: a run
  started by hand (`POST threads/start`), through another assistant's request tool or by a message
  typed while a run worked, and every turn that answers such a message, also in a run a schedule or
  someone else started. When it acts for someone else, such as the account the agent answers to, the
  server is left out with `assistant-mcp-initiator-only`; organization credentials are unaffected.
  Connections and tool lists are cached per person only. Administrators test and sync such a
  server with their own connection (`POST admin/mcp-servers/{id}/connection/authorize`; `GET` and
  `DELETE .../connection` then read and remove that own connection), count the personal connections
  and revoke them all. Personal connections unused for `ConnectionRetention` lose their tokens, which
  are revoked; a person's consent to background use stays on the row, as after a disconnect. The MCP
  maintenance also asks `INhAiPrincipalFactory` about every owner of a personal connection, with the
  whole application as subject, in batches of 100 and a pass at most every hour: a person it no longer
  resolves (removed, or no longer allowed to sign in) loses the tokens the same way, audited as
  `McpConnectionDisconnected` with `owner-unresolved`. A host with its own principal factory resolves
  every person who may use the assistant for that subject too. `ToolInvoked` names whose credential a call carried in
  `McpConnectionOwner`.
- Every administration change is a content-free audit event
  (`AdminContextUpdated`, `AdminAgent*`, `AdminMcpServer*`, `AdminMcpToolUpdated`).

Tool calls whose arguments arrive without the `input` envelope still run through the
governed function once. An envelope mixed with other properties, or arguments that
cannot be bound, completes the tool call with `resultCode` `ai-tool-input-invalid` and
a message that names only the unexpected property names, so the model can retry in
the same turn. Unexpected tool exceptions complete with `ai-tool-failed` and are
logged as warnings with tool ID, version, turn ID and exception type only.

When a turn reaches `MaxToolCallsPerTurn`, or the daily tool budget refuses a call, the
assistant does not end silently: it makes one more model call with tool choice `none`,
the tool results gathered so far and an instruction to answer with what is known and name
what is missing, and streams that answer as normal `message.delta`. `turn.completed` still
carries `assistant-tool-call-limit-reached` (an exhausted budget still ends with the
`assistant-budget-exhausted` `error` event) so the UI can show a notice. Any tool call in
the closing answer is refused without running. Follow-up turns replay each earlier
assistant message with a `<tool-call-summary>` block marked as data: at most ten lines of
tool id, version, an argument preview of 160 characters (redacted for confidential and
restricted tools), status, result code and a truncation flag. Results are never replayed
or logged, and the summary counts against the history budget.

A provider error inside the model stream ends the turn as `failed` with
`assistant-model-unavailable`; the provider's HTTP retry does not cover such errors. A
transient one (`server_is_overloaded`, `server_error` or `rate_limit_exceeded`) that
arrives before the model wrote text or called a tool is retried once after a short wait,
so a brief overload does not reach the user. A failed conversation stays open: the next
message starts a new turn in the same conversation or agent thread; only an archived
conversation takes no messages.

## Situational and page context

Give the model the moment and the user without a tool call. `UseTimeZone("Europe/Amsterdam")`
sets the zone of the date, weekday and time the library adds to every turn (UTC by
default). Implement `INhAssistantTurnContextProvider` for short facts such as the user's
name, roles or active division, built from the authenticated context and the
application's own data only, and register it with `UseTurnContextProvider<T>()`; several
providers are allowed. Facts are cut off at 20 per turn, 2,000 characters in total, 60
characters per label and 300 per value. A failing provider is skipped for the turn and
logged with its exception type only.

Clients send the page they show as `clientContext` with `POST messages`: `route` (200
characters), optional `title` (120) and at most five `entities` (`type` in dash-case, `id`
of at most 64 characters, optional `label` of 120). The server validates again, cuts off
long text and drops a value of the wrong shape without answering `400`. The context is
stored with the user message and used again when the turn resumes after an approval.

Both arrive as the "Situation" and "User's screen" blocks after the composed instructions,
marked as data, not instructions. They are not part of the
prompt hash or the approval binding, so another moment or page never invalidates a
pending approval. Audit events carry only `ContextFactCount`, `PageEntityCount` and
`HadPageContext`.

## Application map

Tell the model which data exists and how it relates, instead of letting it search first:
`ConfigureAgentContext(agentId, context => context.UseApplicationMap())`. Unlike
`ConfigureAgent`, it does not make the agent run on its own, so chat agents use it too. Every
turn of the agent then reads an `# Application map` block after the instructions and before
the situation data: one line per resource the acting person may read, with its title,
summary, operations and relations, from the API bridge gateway and the sources added with
`AddApplicationMapSource<T>()`. A resource is listed only when the turn offers a tool that
reads it, such as the gateway's `query` or `get`, so it never points at data the turn cannot
read. The map is marked as data, cut off at `MaxApplicationMapCharacters` (4,000, at most
16,000) with a note to use `search-resources`, read once per turn, and left out when a
source fails or exceeds `ApplicationMapTimeout` (2 seconds). It is not part of the prompt
hash or the approval binding; tool audit events carry its `ApplicationMapHash`. Keep the
application context for the domain's terms, processes and priorities; the map lists the
entities and stays current with every release and permission.

## Retrieved context

Give an agent the documents that match each question with `UseRetrievedContext` on the same
`ConfigureAgentContext` call, for example `context.UseApplicationMap().UseRetrievedContext(
retrieval => retrieval.Sources("project-documents"))`. The `nh-ai-context-retrieval` rule covers
the sources, their authorization, the query and the bounds. The `# Retrieved context` block is the
last turn data, after the situation and the user's screen; like the map it is data outside the
prompt hash and the approval binding, and tool audit events carry its `RetrievedContextHash`.

## Sharing, live updates and notifications

A conversation keeps exactly one owner. The owner shares it with `POST
conversations/{id}/share-link`, which returns a token the client turns into a link;
the token is protected with ASP.NET Data Protection, so hosts with several instances
share their key ring as for MCP secrets. A new link replaces the old one and `DELETE
share-link` revokes it; people who joined stay until the owner removes them. A caller
joins with `POST conversations/{id}/join` only when the token matches, the caller
belongs to the owner's tenant and passes the agent's policy. Register
`UseParticipantDirectory<T>()` to let owners invite colleagues directly: the
directory searches people the caller may invite (`participant-candidates`) and
resolves them again on `POST participants`; it never receives an id from the client
it has not approved itself. `NhAssistantLimits.MaxParticipantsPerConversation`
(20 by default) bounds a conversation. Joins of one conversation, by link, invitation
or a thread's subject, take turns under the platform's transaction lock, so parallel
requests of one person add one row without a failed insert and parallel joins never
pass the limit. A participant leaves with `DELETE
conversations/{id}`, the owner deletes it for everyone. Names come from
`INhAssistantDisplayNameResolver` (default: the `name`, given and family name, name,
`preferred_username` and e-mail claims) and are normalized before they are stored.

Every person runs their own turns: the sender's permissions, budget and invocation
context apply, the user message records its author, and the model receives each user
message as `[name] text` plus a "Shared conversation" data block after the
situation. Only the person whose turn created a proposal decides it
(`assistant-approval-forbidden`); the owner or that person can cancel
(`assistant-turn-forbidden`). The owner and each participant keep their own read
position (`POST conversations/{id}/read`), which only moves forward; the list
returns `lastMessageSequence` and `lastReadSequence`, so a conversation is unread
while the first is higher. Conversations from before sharing count as read.
Sharing, joining, inviting, removing and leaving are content-free audit events
(`Conversation*`).

`MapNewHeapAssistant` maps the SignalR hub at `NhAssistantOptions.HubPath`
(`/hub/assistant` by default; empty turns live updates off). A connection joins
the group of its authenticated actor, and the server decides per event who belongs to
the conversation, so a removed participant stops receiving updates. The hub sends
`ConversationChanged`, `ConversationRead` (to the reader only), `ConversationRemoved`
and `ConversationEvent` with the same turn events the starting request streams plus
`message.created`. NewHeap hosts read the bearer token and active division from the
query string below `/hub`; other hosts must accept `access_token` there. Updates
reach the instance that runs the turn and use the host's SignalR backplane when there
is one; clients reload snapshots after every reconnect.

Configure Web Push with `ConfigurePush` or `NewHeap:AI:Assistant:Push`: a VAPID key
pair from `NhAssistantWebPushKeys.Generate()` kept as a secret and a `mailto:` or
https `Subject`. Startup fails on invalid keys. Notifications are on by default and
every user can turn them off for all devices (`PUT notifications`). A browser
subscribes with `PUT notifications/push-subscription`; the endpoint must be https on a
host in `AllowedEndpointHosts` (the Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari push services by
default), so the server never posts to an address a client chose. When a turn that ran
at least `MinimumTurnDuration` (10 seconds) completes or fails, the owner and
participants receive an RFC 8291 encrypted, VAPID-signed notification; an approval
notifies only the person who decides it, and cancelled turns stay silent. The payload
carries the conversation id, a kind and short localized texts with the conversation
title (`IncludeConversationTitle`); never messages or tool data. Delivery happens after
the final event and never fails the turn; subscriptions reported as gone are removed.

## Files in model turns

Let turns read the application's files with `UseFileSource<T>()`, where `T` implements
`INhAssistantFileSource`. The application keeps the files, decides who may read them and how
sensitive they are; the assistant keeps references and hashes only. Without a source turns take no
files, and every file is refused with `assistant-files-unavailable`. Declare on the model profile
which media types its model reads itself, and give the files people upload, which are
`Confidential` by default, a fallback profile that permits them:

```csharp
services.AddNewHeapPlatformAI(ai => ai
    .AddChatProfile("project-assistant-chat", profile => profile
        .UseKeyedClient("project-model")
        .RequireCapabilities(NhAiModelCapability.FunctionCalling)
        .WithStreaming(NhAiStreamingPolicy.Allowed)
        .PermitDataClassifications(NhAiDataClassification.Internal)
        .AcceptMediaTypes(NhAiMediaTypes.Pdf, NhAiMediaTypes.Png, NhAiMediaTypes.Jpeg)
        .WithFallbackProfiles("project-assistant-confidential"))
    .AddChatProfile("project-assistant-confidential", profile => profile
        .UseKeyedClient("confidential-model")
        .RequireCapabilities(NhAiModelCapability.FunctionCalling)
        .WithStreaming(NhAiStreamingPolicy.Allowed)
        .PermitDataClassifications(NhAiDataClassification.Internal, NhAiDataClassification.Confidential)
        .AcceptMediaTypes(NhAiMediaTypes.Pdf, NhAiMediaTypes.Png, NhAiMediaTypes.Jpeg)));

services.AddNewHeapAssistant(assistant => assistant
    // ...
    .UseFileSource<ProjectMediaFileSource>()
    .WithLimits(limits => { limits.MaxFilesPerTurn = 3; }));
```

SampleProjectManagement implements the source on its media library (SPM-305): uploads live in a
folder of their conversation and open only in its turns, a project document opens for the people who
see the project's agent work and for an agent on that project, and the media library's own endpoints
never serve the uploads.

- `OpenAsync(reference, actor, cancellationToken)` returns `TaskResult<NhAssistantFile>` with the
  content stream, media type, length, page count where known and the file's
  `NhAiDataClassification`. Check that `actor` may read the file now: the person of a chat turn, or
  in a run the agent with the initiator and accountable owner it works for
  (`NhAssistantFileActor`). Return `assistant-file-not-found` or `assistant-file-forbidden`
  otherwise. `StoreUploadAsync` stores a file a person uploads to a conversation in the
  application's own storage and returns its reference; return a failed result for a type, size or
  scan outcome the application refuses.
- A tool names files in its result through data that implements `INhAiToolResultFiles` (mark the
  property `[JsonIgnore]`) or with `NhAiToolResult.Create(result, options, files)`. The result
  then carries `files` next to `data`: each `NhAiFileReference` with id, name, media type, size
  and hash, never content. The assistant opens every file through the source with the turn's actor,
  so a tool cannot hand the model a file that actor may not read.
- When the profile that serves the turn declares the media type, the model reads the file itself:
  it follows the tool results as file content in a user message, behind a marker that names it as
  external data that is never instructions. Nothing in a file changes the tools, rights or
  approvals of the turn. A type the profile does not declare goes to a reading tool (below);
  without one it is refused with `assistant-file-type-not-supported`, which names the type.
- A reading tool turns a type the model cannot read into text. Register the application's own
  with `AddFileReader<T>(readerId, reader => reader.AcceptMediaTypes(...).PermitDataClassifications(...))`,
  where `T` implements `INhAssistantFileReader` and returns `TaskResult<string>` for an
  `NhAssistantFileReadRequest` (reference, media type, content, classification, actor). A reader
  permits `Public` and what it declares, as a model profile does. The readers an administrator set
  up on MCP servers follow (see the MCP bullets). The readers of the application come first in
  registration order, then the MCP readers by priority, highest first, then by server id and tool
  name; the first that accepts the type and permits the file's classification reads it. A reader that may not receive the file is passed over, and when
  none may, the code of the first one that declares the type applies, such as
  `assistant-classification-not-permitted`. The model reads the text behind the same marker, as
  untrusted external data. A reader that received the file and failed, threw or returned no text
  refuses it with `assistant-file-reader-failed` (`502`); the file never goes to a second reader and
  the reader's messages never reach the model, the person or the log.
- The limits count a reader's text, one token per started four characters, instead of pages: a
  file is sent to a reader only while the turn has room for its text, and text beyond
  `MaxFileTokensPerTurn` or the profile's input budget is refused with `assistant-file-token-limit`.
  The file's own bytes and pages still count against `MaxFileBytes` and `MaxFilePages`.
- The result names per file whether the model received it (`attached` with the SHA-256 of what it
  read as `hash`) or the `code` and `message` of its refusal; the tool call itself succeeds.
- `NhAssistantLimits` bounds every file and turn: `MaxFileBytes` (20 MB), `MaxFilePages` (100,
  when the source reports a page count), `MaxFilesPerTurn` (5; the files of one result count
  together) and `MaxFileTokensPerTurn` (100,000; a file counts 1,000 tokens per page, an image
  one page and a file without a page count one page per started 100 KB, also within the profile's
  input budget). Each refusal has its own code: `assistant-file-too-large`,
  `assistant-file-too-many-pages`, `assistant-file-count-limit` and `assistant-file-token-limit`.
  An agent or skill can only lower them (`AcceptsFiles(limits => ...)`, `NhAssistantFileLimits`).
- The turn takes the highest classification of its files, its agent and its skill. A model call
  that carries a more sensitive file goes to the fallback profile that permits it; a file no profile
  of the chain may receive is refused with `assistant-classification-not-permitted`.
- The chat assistant, an agent without run settings, accepts files at once. An agent configured
  with `ConfigureAgent`, and each of its skills, accepts none until it is switched on with
  `AcceptsFiles()` or in the administration; see the agent-runs rule. Otherwise files are refused
  with `assistant-files-not-accepted`.
- Messages and tool calls keep the reference, name, media type and hashes of a file, never its
  content. A later turn opens the files of the history it replays again through the source with its
  own actor, newest first and each file once, within the same limits on their own; a file it cannot
  open is named in its place with the reason.
- `FileRead` and `FileRefused` business events carry `FileId`, `FileMediaType`, `FileHash`, how
  the file reached the turn as `ObjectId` (`NhAssistantFileOrigins`) and, for a tool result, the
  tool and invocation. `FileReaderId` names the reading tool that read, refused or failed the file:
  the reader id, or `mcp.<server>` with `McpConnectionOwner` for an MCP server; for a file a reader
  read, `FileHash` is the SHA-256 of the content the reader received. File content and a reader's
  text never reach logs, audit or usage records.

A reading tool of the application, registered next to the file source. NewHeap's packages carry no
document library; the sample's `OfficeDocumentReader` (SPM-305) is an example to copy, which reads
Word and Excel documents with DocumentFormat.OpenXml in the application's own process:

```csharp
services.AddNewHeapAssistant(assistant => assistant
    // ...
    .UseFileSource<ProjectMediaFileSource>()
    .AddFileReader<OfficeDocumentReader>("office-documents", reader => reader
        .AcceptMediaTypes(NhAiMediaTypes.Docx, NhAiMediaTypes.Xlsx)
        .PermitDataClassifications(NhAiDataClassification.Internal, NhAiDataClassification.Confidential)));
```

- Bound what a reader unpacks, such as OpenXml's `OpenSettings.MaxCharactersInPart`, and return a
  failed result for a damaged document instead of text cut off; the turn's limits count the text.

People attach files to a chat message in two steps. First the client uploads each file to the
conversation with `POST {prefix}/conversations/{id}/files`: `multipart/form-data` with one file part
named `file` and the header `X-NH-Assistant-Upload: 1`, which a cross-site form cannot send, so the
endpoint keeps the posture of the JSON endpoints under the same access policy. The endpoint checks, in
this order, the conversation and the agent's policy (as for a message), a file source
(`assistant-files-unavailable`), an agent that accepts files (`assistant-files-not-accepted`), one
named, non-empty file part (`assistant-file-upload-invalid`), an accepted media type whose content
starts as files of that type do (`assistant-file-type-not-accepted`) and the agent's `MaxFileBytes`
(`assistant-file-too-large`). Only then does `StoreUploadAsync` receive the file, with the name
without its path, the media type lowercase and `NhAssistantFileUpload.Classification`; it answers the
`NhAiFileReference` the endpoint returns. A refusal of the source answers
`assistant-file-upload-refused` (422) unless it is `assistant-file-too-large`,
`assistant-file-type-not-accepted` or `assistant-files-unavailable`; an exception or an invalid
reference answers `assistant-file-upload-failed` (503) and logs only its type. Then the message carries
the references in `files` of `POST conversations/{id}/messages` (`NhAssistantSendMessageRequest.Files`),
at most the agent's files per turn, and the turn opens them as described above.

```csharp
services.AddNewHeapAssistant(assistant => assistant
    // ...
    .UseFileSource<ProjectMediaFileSource>()
    .ConfigureUploads(uploads =>
    {
        // PDF, PNG, JPEG, Word and Excel by default; no types switches uploads off.
        uploads.AcceptMediaTypes(NhAiMediaTypes.Pdf, NhAiMediaTypes.Png, NhAiMediaTypes.Jpeg);
        // Confidential by default: the profile, or a fallback, must permit it.
        uploads.DefaultClassification = NhAiDataClassification.Confidential;
    }));
```

- Store the classification of an upload with the file and report it from `OpenAsync`; raise it when
  the application knows the content is more sensitive. Uploads that no message ends up carrying stay
  in the application's storage under its own retention.
- The endpoint lowers the request body limit of an upload to the agent's `MaxFileBytes` plus 16 KB,
  but never raises the server's own limit (Kestrel's `MaxRequestBodySize`, 30 MB by default); raise
  that one too when `MaxFileBytes` is larger.
- `GET status` and `GET agents` give each agent `uploads` (`NhAssistantAgentUploadsDto`) with the
  accepted media types, the largest file and the most files of one message, or `null` when people can
  attach nothing to it, so a client checks a file before it uploads it.
- The conversation shows a person's attachments as `file` parts (`NhAssistantFilePartDto`) with name,
  media type and size, also in the live `message.created` event; never the content, the application's
  id or a hash. Files a tool returned stay named in that call's result, which follows the viewer's
  rights to it. A message with attachments in a busy agent thread is refused with
  `assistant-conversation-busy` instead of waiting for the next run, whose queue carries text only.

## Agent threads

An agent that runs on its own (see the agent-runs rule) keeps one thread per agent and
subject in the same `nhai` schema. A thread is a conversation of kind `thread`; it never
appears in a person's conversation list, and nobody owns it: the subject's access
resolver decides on every request who reads it, who types in it and who decides its
proposals. A person who types in a thread starts a turn in which that person is the
initiator; such a turn is bound to the request like a chat turn, its approvals are
always inline, and a message that arrives while a run is active waits for the next
run (`202 Accepted` with a receipt). Request-bound turns end with the request, and
their cancellation reaches only the process that runs them; work that must outlive a
request belongs in an agent run.

## Context for a reviewed MCP tool

When a remote service needs the conversation to answer, keep its model-facing schema
small (for example only `question`) and send the context as request metadata instead.
Register the reviewed tool in code with `AddMcpContextBinding(new
NhAssistantMcpContextBinding(serverId, serverUrl, remoteName))`. The binding applies
only while an administrator connects the server under that id and URL; any other
server, URL or tool never receives the context. Each call then carries `_meta` key
`com.newheap/assistant-context` with the acting agent, the accountable person, the
conversation, turn and tool invocation ids, the approval and proposal ids of an approved
call and, unless `IncludeSnapshot` is off, a bounded snapshot: the first question plus
the latest completed user and assistant text within `NhAssistantConversationSnapshotRequest`
(`MaxRecentMessages`, `MaxBytes`, `MaxMessageBytes`), with omitted messages and bytes.
Code that needs the snapshot elsewhere inside a tool call uses
`INhAssistantConversationSnapshotProvider` with the call's invocation context. It
verifies the running call, the run, the accountable actor's access and the active turn
itself, and never returns instructions, tool calls or results, approvals, page context
or output of the running turn, also not text written before an approval pause.

## Avoid

- Calling `AddNewHeapAssistant` before `AddNewHeapPlatformAIAspNet` or replacing the
  invocation gate, budget, idempotency or evidence manager afterwards; startup fails.
- Registering or replacing `INhAiToolDiscoveryPolicy` for the assistant; discovery
  stays owned by the application or the API bridge.
- Adding agent-specific copies of tools to bypass approval, or approving on behalf
  of the user from code.
- Writing prompts, messages, tool arguments or results to logs, `INhAiAuditSink`,
  usage records or `INhAssistantBusinessAuditSink`; those receive identifiers,
  versions, codes and timestamps only.
- Applying the library migrations to a shared database without an explicit
  deployment decision; `RunMigrations` is off by default.
- Relying on `POST cancel` across nodes; it reaches turns in the same process, and
  an abandoned running turn is recovered after its deadline.
- Trusting remote MCP annotations such as `readOnlyHint`; they are hints for the
  administrator only. Mark a remote tool read-only only after reviewing it.
- Forwarding user tokens to hosts outside `ForwardUserTokenHosts`, or allowing plain
  http, link-local or metadata addresses for MCP servers.
- Setting `headlessUse` to `organization` for a server whose credential lets an agent
  do more than the people it works for may; background runs then act with it.
- Sharing the HS256 signing key with a first-party MCP server so that it can validate delegated
  tokens; sign asymmetrically and let it validate with the published keys. Letting the assistant's
  own host `Accept` delegated MCP tokens on more than its MCP endpoint.
- Writing a secret resolver that maps a reference name to arbitrary settings, files or
  environment variables; a name selects one secret of one source.
- Forwarding a person's own NewHeap token from an application's credential provider; exchange it
  for a token of the MCP server instead, and keep the provider's client secret in the secrets file.
- Using an organization connection for a system that must know who acts, such as a mailbox or a
  calendar; let each person connect (`connectionScope: user`).
- Connecting an organization `oauth` server with a personal or administrator account;
  everyone using the server's agents acts as it. Connect a service account and name it in
  `organizationAccountLabel`.
- Confirming an authorization server that the administration did not expect, or adding
  the host's own pages to `ReturnOrigins` from configuration that users control.
- Putting permissions, approval rules or scope decisions in the application context or
  the preferences; they explain the domain and shape style only.
- Listing the application's entities in the application context; use the application map.
- Deciding access from page context or provider facts. Entity ids on the user's screen are
  search hints; authorization and division scope stay with the tools and the gate.
- Putting secrets, tokens or model input into provider facts.
- Sharing a conversation that holds confidential tool results with people who may not
  see them: participants read the whole history, including result previews.
- Returning people of another tenant from `INhAssistantParticipantDirectory`, or
  trusting an actor id from the client without resolving it in the directory.
- Letting a participant decide another participant's approval, or treating the
  conversation owner as the actor of every turn.
- Committing VAPID private keys, widening `AllowedEndpointHosts` to arbitrary hosts or
  putting message content into notification texts.
- Binding the assistant context to a server id without its reviewed URL, asking the model
  to repeat conversation text as tool arguments, or treating the metadata as
  authorization on the remote side.
- Returning file content, base64 or extracted text in a tool's data to show the model a document;
  return references and let the file source open them with the turn's actor.
- Checking access to a file only in the tool that names it; `OpenAsync` decides for every turn,
  also a later one with another actor.
- Declaring media types in `AcceptMediaTypes` that the model behind the profile cannot read, or
  reporting a file as less sensitive than it is.
- Setting an MCP server up as reader with a `maxClassification` above what may leave the platform
  for that server, or letting a reader of the application send files to an external service
  without limiting its classifications with `PermitDataClassifications`.
- Showing a reader's own error messages or logging its text: a document can carry anything.
- Storing an upload without `NhAssistantFileUpload.Classification`, or trusting the declared media
  type of an application-specific upload type without checking its content in `StoreUploadAsync`.

## Verification

Drive turns with `NhAiScriptedChatClient` against real SQL Server and PostgreSQL:
a read-only turn with one tool call, a mutation that pauses for approval and
resumes after approve, a reject that closes without executing, an expired
proposal, an exhausted daily budget, the tool-call limit, cancel and a disabled
flag. Script a provider error inside the stream with
`RespondWithProviderError("server_is_overloaded")` and assert that one retry answers, that
a repeated or non-transient error fails the turn with `assistant-model-unavailable`, and
that the failed conversation accepts the next message. At the tool-call limit, assert a closing answer from a request with tool choice
`none` that carries every call's result, no further tool execution, and a follow-up
turn whose history holds the tool-call summary but no result content. Send one call with flat arguments and one with `input` mixed with another
property, and assert the first succeeds and the second returns `ai-tool-input-invalid`
before a corrected retry succeeds. Assert that no prompt, argument, result or answer text reaches the audit,
usage and business sinks or logs, that approval is bound to the proposal hash and
owner, and that the SSE event and JSON property names match the contract.
For administration, assert version conflicts, the admin policy, the seed behavior and
the composed instruction order with an injection attempt in the custom instructions.
For situational and page context, assert the block order and markers, the limits, that
an invalid `clientContext` is ignored, that a failing provider does not stop the turn,
that the prompt hash and a pending approval survive another page, and that facts and
page text never reach audit or logs (SPM-254).
For MCP, use an official SDK server (in memory or Streamable HTTP): tools are off after
sync and visible only to the assigned agent after activation, mutations pause for
approval, schema changes disable tools, blocked hosts are rejected and secrets are
absent from responses, logs and audit. For background runs, assert on both providers
that a `never` server is not contacted, an `organization` server is offered and
called through a code grant or a person's rights, `requiredPolicy` is evaluated for
that person, an approved deferred MCP proposal executes once, and a server set back to
`never` fails it with `assistant-mcp-headless-not-allowed` without a call. For OAuth, run `NhAiTestAuthorizationServer` with an `NhAiTestProtectedResource` in
front of the MCP server and assert on both providers that nothing is pinned without
confirmation, client credentials request one token for the resource, `insufficient_scope`
steps up within the allowed scopes, an authorization completes only for its starter with
the admin policy after the `state`, `iss` and expiry checks, concurrent renewals send one
refresh request, a refused refresh requires reauthorization, another issuer suspends the
connection and disconnecting revokes the tokens (SPM-299). For personal connections, assert that
a person without one gets the `connection.required` event and part and no tools, that each
person's turn and each colleague in a shared conversation uses their own account, that step-up asks
to connect again, that a run uses the connection only with consent and that an approved proposal
fails as not connected after the person disconnected (SPM-300). For a
`personal` server, assert on both providers that it is skipped without consent, that
every request then carries a fresh delegated token of the person with the invocation
marker and the server's origin, that a withdrawn consent or a changed URL stops it, and
that a refused, unbound or failing issuer sends nothing. For secret references, rotate
the configured or resolved value between two connections and assert that names with
`:` or `..` are refused. SPM-245, SPM-246, SPM-247, SPM-250, SPM-251 and
SPM-252 and SPM-254 are the executable references. SPM-249 is the end-to-end reference: one agent
over the API bridge and curated tools, an administrator agent with an MCP tool, and a
viewer who is offered no mutating tools.
For sharing, assert on both providers that a participant of another tenant never
reaches the conversation, read positions only move forward, concurrent joins of one
person add one row without an EF Core error log and concurrent joins of different people
stay within the participant limit; over HTTP that a wrong or revoked token fails,
the model sees named user messages, the owner cannot decide a participant's approval,
another participant cannot cancel, removal stops access and live updates, and the hub
rejects anonymous connections (SPM-263). For push, check the RFC 8291 test vector,
a verifiable VAPID token, the endpoint allow-list, the notification rules, an
encrypted delivery without message content, the opt-out and the removal of a gone
subscription (SPM-264). For the MCP context, read `_meta` in the server's call handler
over the official transport: the reviewed tool receives the identities and snapshot, the
same tool under another server id or URL receives nothing, an approved call carries its
approval, and the snapshot refuses another person, another invocation or run, a stale
turn and calls outside a tool call while leaving out output of the running turn and
reporting cut text as omitted bytes (SPM-266).

For the application map, assert that an agent with `UseApplicationMap` reads the entries of the tools its turn offers between the instructions and the situation, in order and within the bound, that a changed map changes its hash but not the prompt, that agents without it and a failing source leave the turn without it, and that the sample's assistant queries the tasks of a project with one gateway call (SPM-289).

For files, script a tool that returns a reference and assert on both providers that the next model
request carries the file after the tool results as file content behind the external-data marker,
that the result names `attached` and the hash, that each limit, an undeclared type, a forbidden or
missing file and a file no profile may receive are refused with their own codes, that a
confidential file moves the model calls to the fallback that permits it, that messages, tool calls,
audit and logs hold references and hashes only, and that a later turn opens the file again with its
own actor and names it when that actor may no longer read it. Over HTTP, upload a file and send it with
a message on both providers and assert the stored classification, the file part of the conversation
without content, id or hash, and the codes of a file too large, a type not accepted, content of
another type, an agent that accepts no files and a caller without access. SPM-305 is the executable
reference on the media library: a PDF a person uploads reaches the model as a file on the confidential
fallback, Word and Excel documents as the example reader's text, another person's conversation cannot
open the upload, and the source refuses a project document to an actor who may not see the project.
SPM-306 shows an agent skill that reads a project's documents through a tool result.

For reading tools, assert on both providers that a type the profile does not read reaches the model as
text from the application's reader behind the marker, that an MCP reader reads what no reader of the
application may read and receives the base64 content, that MCP readers are asked by priority, then by
server id and tool name, that a file above a reader's classification and a personal server without
the person's consent send nothing, that a personal OAuth reader the person has not connected shows
the connection card in the person's turn and none in a headless run, that a failing reader refuses
its file with `assistant-file-reader-failed` without a second reader, that the reader's text counts
against `MaxFileTokensPerTurn`, and that audit and logs hold the reader id, file id and hash, never
the content or the text. Prove a migration that moves data, such as `McpReaders`, on both providers
from the earlier schema up and back down.

For retrieved context, assert that the sample's assistant reads the project descriptions of the
person's active division that match the question, after the situation, never those of another
division, and that audit and logs carry its hash but not its content (SPM-291).
